instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Twelve goals and eight assists from the left in a double-winning side, and a place in the PFA team of the year; the one season he played to the level Lyon had sold.
Thirteen goals and Chelsea’s player of the season — a second year at the level of 2009/10 rather than a step past it, which is what turning thirty during it argues for.
Thirty-one and visibly declining, dropped to the fringe under Villas-Boas; the two-season peak was over.
A Champions League winner and Euro 2004 finalist starting at right back for the record-breaking Chelsea defence; positionally excellent, offensively limited.
Seven starts before the double leg break in September 2000 that ended his career.
Three starts in a brief spell at Tottenham; he barely played top-flight football that season.

Scotland’s captain and a genuinely excellent passer and organiser; his Blackburn spell is remembered as a disappointment, which is a claim about the team and his fitness rather than about the footballer.
Thirty-one and an ever-present in Birmingham’s ninth-place season; still an excellent organiser and passer, with the legs going.
His first full season and an immediate jump: left-sided, quick and much the most comfortable passer in the Liverpool back four.
Nine goals in sixteen starts after the move; a prolific second-tier scorer who was ordinary in the top flight.
Nine goals in sixteen starts after the move; a prolific second-tier scorer who was ordinary in the top flight.
Ten starts; the knee and calf problems that ended his career at 28 had begun.
Four starts at 32; out of the Liverpool side rather than injured.
Twenty-three and a squad forward at Roma, six goals in ten starts; the same physical centre-forward as the Villa rows, not yet as reliable.
Thirty-one and plainly slowing in his last Bolton season; the trickery survived, the influence did not.
Thirty-one and down to twelve starts; the honest, limited full back of the Liverpool rows with the legs gone.
Four starts only; injury, not a drop in level.
Seven starts; the injuries that ended his career at 26, not a drop in level.
Rated on the player rather than the Spurs output: a Champions League-winning holding midfielder and Germany international, already past his physical peak at 28.
Twenty-one starts in a relegation season, at 30 and past his best. Note: the docs anchor puts his 1993/94 at 76 while the reviewed row here reads 73 — flagged, not changed.
Five starts; the first of the achilles and hamstring seasons that finished his career early.
A poor first season in a chaotic, relegated club, but an Argentina centre-back whose ability was plainly above what the year showed.
PFA Team of the Year as captain of a fifth-placed side; the composed, ball-playing defender Newcastle had paid for finally showed up week after week.
An ever-present in the meanest defence outside the top four that season; big, aggressive and dominant in the air, and briefly an England contender.
A poor season captaining a relegated side, with errors and discipline problems; the Birmingham form did not travel.
Liverpool’s player of the season in a bad year for the club; the reading of the game and the ball retention had both caught up with the effort.
Thirty-five and a stand-in at Sunderland; a clear decline from the City years.
Footballer of the Year; world-class talent barely diminished at 32.
Thirty-five, seven starts at Sunderland; the touch and the passing were still there, the rest was not.
The best pure ball-winner in the league that season, which is what a mid-season move to Tottenham for twelve million pounds was paying for.
Squeezed out at Tottenham and no longer the ball-winner Wigan sold; the drop is real, not rotation.
World class: pace, strength and reading combined, and in 1998/99 in the conversation for the best centre-back in Europe. Rated above Adams (88) and just under Ferdinand 2007/08 (91).
An Achilles rupture cost him the first half of the season and he was sold that summer; still world class when he played, a point off his peak.
Thirty-one and a first-choice centre-half in Serie A; three points down on the Manchester United peak, and still elite.
